question: Is the fresh four-head program necessary in the reverse direction, and does its single occupied M11 weight mode mediate the resulting behavioral effect?
evidence_status: Prospective manipulation and rescue test. Forward sufficiency, four-head interactions, frozen weight modes, occupancy, and layerwise transport are open. No reverse four-head removal, occupied-mode removal, or head-removal-plus-M11-rescue outcome on v23 has been opened.

searched: all v15-v23 is/was head removal, reader loss, M11 rescue, source-writer, factor, and mediation priors/results
v23 aligned four-head confirmation, frozen weight tensor, occupancy transport, and L8/L9/L11 transport receipts
earlier v17 complete A11/M11 reader-loss and full-output rescue
prior_art.novelty: Earlier work rescued complete reader/module outputs and established forward donor transfer. No prior test reverses this prospectively frozen four-head union on the aligned v23 bank and compares complete M11-factor rescue with a one-dimensional weight-defined occupied-mode rescue.
prior_art.known_lessons: A decoded direction is not necessarily a removable causal carrier. The leading mode is eligible only because it is weight-defined before this run, occupies 97.1% of realized response on split-stable data, and belongs to a separately confirmed causal head union. Full-factor rescue is required as the positive-control ceiling.

frozen_design.population: All 64 aligned v23 rows; target behavior uses the capability-frozen 30 jointly correct A1/A2 rows, with P, C, and reporter halves separate.
frozen_design.head_removal: Start from each donor prompt and replace the inclusive-prefix c_proj input slices of L8H1/L9H1/L9H4/L11H3 by their matched base values. Score donor-minus-removed margin as reverse recovery toward the paired base state.
frozen_design.factor_ceiling_rescue: Capture the native-donor and head-removed M11 bilinear factor states. Repeat head removal and add the complete corresponding M11 Down-weighted factor difference to M11's output. This is the registered mediation ceiling; it does not alter the residual skip carrying the removed heads.
frozen_design.occupied_mode_rescue: Let u be the leading reader-mode left singular vector of the frozen weight tensor, mapped through the frozen reader basis into a unit vector f over 4,608 M11 factors. Repeat head removal and add only Down[f f^T(H_donor-H_removed)] to M11 output.
frozen_design.occupied_mode_removal: On the native donor path, subtract Down[f f^T(H_donor-H_base)] from M11 output. This tests necessity of the paired target change's occupied factor component independently of head removal.
frozen_design.no_op: A donor-to-donor four-head self patch must be exact.

predictions.pred_a_authority_hooks_self_patch_finite: All hashes, exact frozen mode reconstruction, hook counts, donor self no-op, finiteness, and seven-forward price pass.
predictions.pred_b_four_head_union_is_selectively_ne: Head removal passes target recovery/direction and P/C leakage bars with positive recovery in both reporter halves.
predictions.pred_c_occupied_mode_rescues_most_of_com: The full-factor rescue recovers >=.50 of head-removal behavior; occupied-mode rescue has cosine >=.95 and signed projection >=.70 relative to that full-factor rescue, with positive half projections.
predictions.pred_d_occupied_mode_is_directly_necessa: Direct occupied-mode removal recovers >=.40 of the four-head removal effect with positive reporter-half projections and P/C leak <=.15.

null: With valid A, B failure rejects bidirectional necessity of the four-head union. C failure means the occupied mode is descriptive but not a sufficient M11 mediator. D failure means the mode cannot be called a directly removable causal carrier even if it rescues a head intervention.
decision: B-D pass promote the writer-to-M11 occupied-mode interface to selective manipulation. B pass/C or D fail preserves the four-head causal circuit but requires a multidimensional or residual-skip-aware mediator before extraction.
